title: DIVE: Subgraph Disagreement for Graph Out-of-Distribution Generalization

problem.claim: Graph machine learning models struggle to generalize when source and target data distributions differ.

gap.claim: Existing methods have only partially addressed simplicity bias and may reinforce reliance on spurious correlations.

contributions.claim: DIVE trains a collection of models to focus on label-predictive subgraphs while encouraging divergence in their subgraph masks.
DIVE uses a regularizer that penalizes overlap among subgraphs extracted by different models.
The method selects models for robust OOD performance using validation accuracy.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The approach was tested on four datasets from the GOOD benchmark and one dataset from the DrugOOD benchmark.
The authors report significant improvement over existing methods, addressing simplicity bias and improving graph machine learning generalization.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph OOD generalization is difficult because training and test distributions can differ.
Simplicity bias can make neural networks rely on spurious correlations, limiting OOD performance.
Existing approaches have had partial success but do not reliably overcome simplicity bias.
DIVE encourages multiple models to identify diverse label-predictive subgraphs by penalizing overlap.
The authors report improved performance across datasets from the GOOD and DrugOOD benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset names, baselines, numerical results, or statistical significance details.
The abstract does not describe the validation protocol or the form of the subgraph masks in detail.
